summary: Qatar grants free visa waivers on arrival to citizens of nearly 90 countries — 90 days within 180 for EU and Schengen-area passports, 30 extendable days for most others including the US, UK and much of Asia and Latin America — and routes the remaining nationalities through the official Hayya platform for a tourist visa.

notes: The UK FCDO says Qatar has zero tolerance for drug offences, even residual amounts, and that some medicines legal elsewhere are controlled or illegal in Qatar. To bring controlled or prescription medication, follow the Ministry of Public Health's steps, including carrying a prescription and a medical report in English or Arabic, issued within the last 6 months; the Ministry runs an online permit service.

The UK FCDO says it is illegal to import, sell or buy vapes and e-cigarette products, including liquids and electronic shisha pipes, whatever the quantity; customs may confiscate them, and using them can lead to arrest, a fine, prison or deportation.

safety.text: Crime is low, but since 8 July 2026 Iran has carried out strikes and retaliatory attacks across the region, including in Qatar, against US military and civilian infrastructure, and further attacks are possible. Expect possible flight cancellations and airspace closures, stay away from security and military sites, and follow local authorities' instructions. Strict laws on alcohol, drugs, public behavior and photography also apply.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says high humidity and severe heat occur from June to September, and that dehydration and heatstroke can be fatal: carry enough water and plan outdoor activity for the cooler hours.

The UK FCDO says only licensed hotels, restaurants and bars can sell alcohol, the legal drinking age is 21, and drinking or being drunk in public is illegal. There is zero tolerance for drink-driving: any amount of alcohol can mean one month to 3 years in prison or a fine of QAR 10,000–50,000, and deportation.

The UK FCDO says to dress modestly in public, including while driving — men and women should cover their shoulders and knees — and that the dress code is strictly enforced in government buildings, healthcare facilities and banks, where you may be refused entry.
The official Hayya app and portal (hayya.qa) is the single place to check visa eligibility, apply for a tourist visa and manage entry. Avoid third-party visa websites.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Qatar?
faq.answer: No advance visa is needed. US passport holders receive a free visa waiver on arrival valid for 30 days, which can be extended through the Ministry of Interior before it expires. Hayya also offers US citizens an optional Visa-Free for US Citizens (F1), applied for online: QAR 76, multiple entry, up to 90 days per visit, for travel within 2 years of approval.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Qatar?
faq.answer: Citizens of EU and Schengen-area countries (plus Switzerland) get a free waiver on arrival allowing up to 90 days within any 180-day period — the most generous tier of Qatar's waiver scheme.

faq.question: What is Hayya and do I need it to enter Qatar?
faq.answer: Hayya (hayya.qa) is Qatar's official entry and visa platform, kept on after the 2022 World Cup. Most visa-waiver nationalities can simply arrive with their passport (Thai, Ukrainian and Pakistani citizens must first book accommodation through Discover Qatar), while nationalities that need a visa apply for the Hayya A1 tourist visa there — QAR 100, with confirmed accommodation required.

faq.question: Can tourists drink alcohol in Qatar?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in licensed venues: the UK FCDO says only licensed hotels, restaurants and bars can sell alcohol and the legal drinking age is 21. Drinking or being drunk in public is illegal and can bring up to 6 months in prison or a fine of up to QAR 3,000, and there is zero tolerance for drink-driving.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Qatar?
faq.answer: Visitors on the 30-day waiver must extend it through the Ministry of Interior before it expires, or they may be fined; no official source we could read states the length of the extension. The 90-in-180-day waiver for EU passports is not extendable beyond its limit.
